method: A code is the number written in base 32, five bits per symbol, using the 32 characters 0-9 and A-Z without I, L, O and U; the digit loop divides by 32 with BigInt arithmetic so any length is exact, letters are emitted in upper case, and zero encodes as a single 0. Leading zeros carry no value and are dropped, so the code is the shortest form of the number and has no fixed width. Decoding is case-insensitive, maps I, i, L and l to 1 and O and o to 0 before lookup, and ignores hyphens and whitespace; any other character is refused with its position. The optional check symbol is the value modulo 37, written with the 32 symbols plus * ~ $ = U (values 32 to 36); when enabled, the last symbol of the code is read as the check symbol, a mismatch is reported with the expected symbol, and the decoded value is withheld. Input is limited to 4,096 characters. Nothing is uploaded, stored or sent.

sources.title: Base 32 by Douglas Crockford (2019-03-04) — the 32-symbol alphabet, the case and I/L/O decoding rules, and the modulo-37 check symbol
